title: Optimize Console Diff Lens and Apply Audit Scribe for Batching & Cache Recipes
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Context: Optimize Console will surface automated recommendations that suggest batching and KV/prefix caching configurations to reduce per-token cost while maintaining latency SLOs. This ticket designs and ships a UI pattern and audit trail that lets engineers review candidate changes, inspect estimated cost/latency deltas, stage safe commits in an isolated sandbox, and reverse an applied config if regressions appear.

Problem statement: Current Optimize recommendations are surfaced as simple suggestions with no strong way to compare before/after or to safely stage an apply. Users need: (1) clearer diffs that highlight operational risk and expected savings, (2) an isolated preview environment for applying configuration changes without impacting live routing, and (3) robust historical traceability with reviewer notes and revert proof.

Goals:
- Create a "Diff Lens" card layout that compares baseline vs proposed config at token/batch and model-level granularity and explains reasoning behind suggested caching/batching knobs.
- Add an "Apply Audit Scribe" that records who staged/applied a recommendation, link to the sandbox run results, and provides one-click revert for safe rollback within the SLA window.
- Surface confidence bands (est. latency percentiles and cost delta) and a short rationale sentence for each recommended knob to improve trust and reduce misapplies.
- Ensure console events generate structured telemetry for regressions and to feed back into Optimize's suggestion model.

Scope (this ticket): UI/UX for card + diff preview + apply history UI, lightweight sandbox orchestration hooks, telemetry contract. Engineering work to actually execute sandboxes and routing fallbacks will be tracked as ENG work (see dependencies).

Out of scope: deep analysis engine changes, new model quantization recommendations, or core runtime changes other than safe staging hooks.

Design notes: We propose a 3-pane Diff Lens layout: left shows current config + live micro-metrics snapshot; center shows human-readable delta and recommended value with a short "why"; right shows expected outcome including estimated token-cost/saving, p50/p95 latency change, and an impact badge (low/med/high). Cards are compact and stackable so multiple recommendations can be compared. The Apply Audit Scribe is a timeline widget attached to each resource (route/model/config) that records staged runs, sandbox run IDs, reviewer notes, and the apply/rollback buttons along with a TTL window for automatic reversion if errors exceed threshold.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria list below.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Overconfidence in point estimates: we mitigate by showing ranges and listing assumptions (sampled seq lengths, traffic split).
- UI complexity: trade concise cards against too much telemetry—we keep the default compact view and an "expand for details" mode.
- Sandbox cost: staged runs will use budgeted reserved capacity; we will implement quotas and warn users about sandbox compute consumption.

Stakeholder reviewers: Console PM, Runtime team lead, Reliability eng, Design lead, Security.

Links to artifacts: design mockups, confluence spec, and prototype PRs listed in attachments.

Notes for eng: telemetry events must include: recommendation_id, baseline_config_hash, proposed_config_hash, sandbox_run_id, apply_user, apply_time, revert_user (if any), revert_time, observed_metrics_snapshot_url.
acceptance_criteria: Diff Lens card surfaces baseline and proposed config side-by-side with highlighted changed knobs
Each recommendation shows estimated cost delta (USD/day) and latency delta (p50/p95) with a confidence band and listed assumptions
Users can stage a recommendation to a sandbox run and view sandbox output (simulated traffic metrics) from within the card
Apply Audit Scribe records staged/apply/revert actions with user, timestamp, and link to sandbox run logs
One-click revert button restores the prior configuration and creates an audit entry; revert succeeds within the configured SLA window
Telemetry events emitted with required keys for downstream Optimize ML feedback loop
updates: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: aligned with Runtime and Reliability on sandbox contract. Runtime requested explicit API for dry-run vs staged-apply. Action: ENG to expose /sandbox/run endpoints (ENG-27011).
2026-03-04 - Design review: Design requested simpler fallback messaging and a compact card mode. Decided to default to compact with 'expand' for details to reduce cognitive load.
2026-03-06 - Security review stub: Security asked for assurance that sandbox runs cannot exfiltrate customer data; Security to sign off on sandbox network egress rules (SEC-389).
2026-03-08 - PM/Eng sync: Agreed telemetry contract and draft schema. Noah to create telemetry ticket.

2026-03-10 - Prototype demo: UX shown to two customers in the beta advisory group; early feedback called for clearer guardrails around automatic applies. We added an explicit 'require approval' toggle for enterprise orgs.
2026-03-12 - Engineering handoff: UI components final; ENG flagged dependency ENG-1842 for audit log persistence. Blocker resolved; moving to implementation sprint 2026-W11.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal dogfood behind feature flag for 10 internal teams (2 weeks). Phase 2: opt-in customer beta with advisory group (4 weeks). Phase 3: gradual rollout to all orgs with enterprise guardrail enforced by default off for orgs without approval workflows. Monitor A/B: adoption, false positive applies, revert rate. Rollback toggle at platform level if revert rate > 3% within 24h.
qa_checklist: Verify compact and expanded card render across screen widths
Validate diff correctness for common recommendation types (batch size, prefix_cache_ttl, cache_mode)
Confirm sandbox run results surface sample traces and aggregated metrics
Test apply + revert flow end-to-end in staging cluster with realistic load
Ensure audit entries persisted and visible across account admins
Smoke telemetry events and confirm fields in analytics pipeline
